description: Documented exceptional events, production milestones and defining moments in festival history. These are not discontinued-festival records.

moments.name: Tomorrowland Belgium 2025 – Mainstage fire and emergency rebuild
moments.venue: De Schorre, Boom, Belgium – Mainstage area
moments.story: On 16 July 2025, a major fire destroyed the original Orbyz Mainstage shortly before the festival opened. Production teams built an alternative mainstage structure in under 48 hours, allowing the festival to open on 18 July. Parts from Metallica's touring production rig were flown in from Austria and used in the replacement setup.
moments.notes: The replacement was not a full reconstruction of the original elaborate stage design; it was an alternative stage solution. The festival's official aftermovie describes the rebuild as completed in less than 48 hours. Contemporary reporting identifies Metallica touring equipment as part of the replacement setup.

moments.name: Woodstock 1969 – Generation-defining gathering
moments.story: More than 450,000 people gathered at Max Yasgur's farm; the event became a defining symbol of the counterculture era.

moments.name: Monterey Pop 1967 – Hendrix burns his guitar
moments.story: Jimi Hendrix's guitar-burning performance and career-making sets by Janis Joplin and Otis Redding became enduring festival history.

moments.name: Live Aid 1985 – The global broadcast
moments.story: The dual-stadium event linked Wembley and Philadelphia in a 16-hour broadcast to more than one billion viewers in 110 countries.

moments.name: Roskilde 2000 – Pearl Jam crowd crush
moments.story: A crowd crush during Pearl Jam's performance killed nine people. It became a defining moment in festival crowd-safety history.

moments.name: Glastonbury 1997 – The Year of the Mud
moments.story: Torrential rain turned the festival into the famous Year of the Mud; the official archive records the conditions and performances.

moments.name: Glastonbury 1995 – Pulp replaces The Stone Roses
moments.story: After The Stone Roses withdrew shortly before the festival, Pulp took their place in a landmark anniversary edition.

moments.name: Glastonbury 2005 – Storms and power failures
moments.story: Severe rain and thunderstorms caused power failures and forced cancellation of the first three scheduled Pyramid Stage acts.

moments.name: Altamont Free Concert 1969 – A tragic turning point
moments.story: The free concert ended in violence and the death of Meredith Hunter during the Rolling Stones' set, becoming a dark counterpoint to Woodstock.

moments.name: Isle of Wight 1970 – Hendrix's final major festival appearance
moments.story: Jimi Hendrix performed at the 1970 Isle of Wight Festival shortly before his death; the edition became a landmark event of the era.

moments.name: Queen at Live Aid – Wembley 1985
moments.story: Queen's Wembley performance became one of Live Aid's defining moments and is celebrated in Wembley Stadium's own history.

moments.name: Woodstock 1994 – The mud returns
moments.story: Heavy rain and mud became the defining visual of the 25th-anniversary Woodstock event.

moments.name: Woodstock 1999 – Festival breakdown
moments.story: The anniversary event ended amid fires, vandalism and reports of violence, becoming a warning about crowd welfare and event management.

moments.name: TomorrowWorld 2015 – Weather and stranded attendees
moments.story: Severe weather and muddy access routes disrupted transport and left many attendees stranded or unable to return to the site.

moments.name: Fyre Festival 2017 – The failed luxury festival
moments.story: The heavily promoted luxury festival collapsed before delivering the promised experience; its promoter was later sentenced for wire fraud.

moments.name: Monsters of Rock 1988 – Donington crowd disaster
moments.story: Two fans died during a crowd surge at the Monsters of Rock festival at Donington Park.

moments.name: Pukkelpop 2011 – Severe storm
moments.story: A severe storm damaged stages and infrastructure, caused fatalities and injuries, and forced the festival to halt.

moments.name: Roskilde 2000 – Safety reforms after tragedy
moments.story: After the crowd crush, organizers published a safety plan covering command structure, audience communication and front-of-stage barriers.

moments.name: Glastonbury 1970 – The first Worthy Farm festival
moments.story: The first Pilton Pop, Folk and Blues Festival at Worthy Farm drew around 1,500 people and laid the foundation for Glastonbury.

moments.name: Woodstock 1969 – Hendrix closes the festival
moments.story: Jimi Hendrix closed Woodstock with his interpretation of the US national anthem, one of the most widely remembered festival performances.
